description: Treat the 14 logical-equivalence rules as an algebra of equivalence-preserving operators and compose them in 5 templates: [contraposition], [implication], [commutative], [contraposition+commutative], [implication+commutative]. Each composition is provably equivalence-preserving (no sampling, no verifier filter needed).

comparison.verdict: matches v12 (best previous mitigation), still below v5 (LogiQA winner) and v6 (ReClor winner)

interpretation: LeRC produces a contrastive corpus that the head learns very cleanly in-distribution (99.80% eval), but the 5 composition templates are too regular for OOD transfer. The diversity-vs-polarity trade-off observed across v8/v9/v10/v11/v12 mitigations is reconfirmed even at the logic layer — rule-composition diversity does not substitute for the wider surface diversity stock T5 provides.
